title: Diagnosis and Repair of a Miswired Three-Way Switch (This Old House)

summary: The video demonstrates a common three-way switch setup where two switches control a single light. The presenter distinguishes single-pole switches from three-way switches, defines the common (black) terminal and the two traveler (brass) terminals, and uses a cutaway to illustrate how a single-pole switch normally completes a circuit. The core of the lesson focuses on diagnosing a miswiring in the dining-room circuit where the common and traveler wires were swapped, likely due to an improper homeowner replacement. After tracing conductors (black and red) from two cables in the box, the speaker shows that the red traveler was tied to the common screw and the black common wire was tied to a brass traveler screw. The fix involves swapping these two wires and ensuring proper screw wrap direction. After restoring power, both switches correctly operate the light, confirming the repair.
